To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

habitat suitability was random from year to year, occupancy probabilities were independent of previous habitat state, and climate and groundwater connectivity were key drivers of local extinction rates, but the effect of groundwater connectivity differed between periods.

1) habitat dynamics were important for determining the local extinction and colonization probabilities of a suite of fishes in a Great Plains stream, 2) groundwater was an important driver of habitat dynamics, and 3) colonization probabilities were generally low during periods of transition between wet and dry conditions, and extinction probabilities were highest.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of a metapopulation of Great Plains stream fish in the Arikarree River, Colorado.
the effects of habitat change on metapopulations, and how this affects the persistence of species.
the effects of habitat dynamics on metapopulations of Great Plains stream fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the present study indicate that the habitat dynamics and species occupancy are closely related, and the species persistence is highly dependent on the habitat change.

the habitat occupancy modeling approach we used here is a valuable tool to incorporate effects of habitat dynamics on metapopulations, and to better inform conservation actions for species of conservation concern.
habitat change is an important factor in determining the persistence of species in metapopulations, especially when the habitat is dynamic and species are sensitive to habitat change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the species in our study were not well suited to the dynamic nature of their habitat and that conservation efforts should focus on protecting groundwater-fed areas.
habitat change, and not site fidelity, was a key driver of local extinction and recolonization for this stream fish assemblages.
the species studied in this study are able to persist in the face of habitat change, and that the species are not necessarily tied to groundwater.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamic habitats are not static, but change in ways that are not predictable from year-to-year and can have important consequences for species persistence.
dynamic habitats are more difficult to conserve than stable habitats, because the species in them must be able to persist in the face of frequent local extinction.
the dynamics of metapopulation systems may be strongly influenced by the dynamic nature of habitat, and that the effects of dynamic habitat can vary among species.
